- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 2–5% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is trending upward but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast slope slightly to reflect sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 3–7% to avoid mean reversion overfit.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/– 0.3), apply smoothing: forecast = weighted average of last 3–5 days + sentiment-adjusted drift.
